items.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I had a flute solo to do with Felix Slatkin or one of the early things with one of the studios.

ctx.x: So the 60s were maybe kind of a difficult decade for jazz, at least in New York.

Also, since my brother was out here, I guess my mother was encouraging me, well why don’t you go try it out there, maybe there’s an opportunity to get into pictures or be close to your brother, and it’ll help you a little bit. So I did get out there. And then I did some T.V. shows out here, playing the studios, I did a few things with some of the studios. In fact he got me one of the earliest things, I’ll tell you about the Frank Sinatra flute earlier. But I had a flute solo to do with Felix Slatkin or one of the…
They say, “Oh he’s a great jazz player but he’s not really ready for this.” What I mean is you don’t get too many chances.
